sentences.text: Trialestes was an extinct genus of crocodylomorphs that lived during the Late Triassic in South America.
It is classified within Sphenosuchia, a group of early crocodylomorph relatives of modern crocodilians.
The holotype specimen PVL 2561 — the specimen the species is based on — was found in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.
The type species Trialestes romeri was named in 1963.
The holotype specimen preserves unambiguous crocodylomorph traits, confirming it is not a dinosaur.
Trialestes was once classified as a dinosaur because it was adapted as a terrestrial, running carnivore.
Trialestes lived during the Carnian stage of the Triassic, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
Researchers Irmis, Nesbitt, and Sues (2013) noted that some material previously referred to Trialestes actually belongs to dinosaurs.
